output.name: Mora
output.myth: Mora was a ptarmigan who could not make up her mind. In summer she wore brown like cliff moss; in winter she went white as drift, and was proud of both. Aun watched her change and laughed until he dropped his string. Hesk heard and said nothing, which is her way. She wound Mora up into the Windward Reach and hung her there, head high, where every house could see. Tavo the Gale came down the cliffs and tried to shake her loose. She held. The Lamp Kite burns to her west for boats lost in the dark, and the Turning Gulls wheel to her east, watching what the wind does first. The Single Mitten hangs north-east of her in the Spindle, the red one Tavo could not keep. Ennu the Kite-Wright says a sensible person changes coat when the weather asks, not when the neighbours do. Old women say it over the nets; young men who swap opinions each morning are Mora's cousins. The bird does not mind. She has been brown and white a thousand times, and no one has talked her out of either.
output.finding: Start at the Lamp Kite, Telvar, and move one fist east along the Windward Reach to find Mora.
